name: Sinte-Manus Romani
sweep_summary: Sinte-Manus Romani (sint1235) is not in the catalog. Both sweep items are Glottolog machine misassignments (the reference records say 'computerized assignment from "mesto"' / '"wesen"'): Diesing & Zec 2016 is about Serbian enclitic placement and Peco 1976 about Serbo-Croatian pitch accent - neither concerns Romani; priority none, not fetched sources. The sweep did locate and read a first-hand open source: Finck 1903, Lehrbuch des Dialekts der deutschen Zigeuner (archive.org, saved with page images checked), whose §§ 3-7 (pp. 4-7) give a full word-stress description for German Sinti: initial stress in nominative nouns and uninflected words, stress on the syllable before Layer-II case/vocative suffixes, theme-vowel stress in the present and final (person-suffix) stress in the preterite, German loans keeping German stress, plus lexical exceptions. Matras 2006 (ELL, open PDF via Wayback) gives the pan-Romani frame: conservative final stress with leftward shift in western/central European dialects. The modern full grammar Holzinger 1993 has no online copy (Harvard print only) and is the high-priority acquisition.

earlier_scan.source_named: Holzinger, Daniel (1993). Das Romanes: Grammatik und Diskursanalyse der Sprache der Sinte. Innsbruck. (full grammar of Sinte Romani; no online copy located)

new_statements.quote: § 4. In den mit einem der Suffixe -ja, -je, -le gebildeten Vokativformen (§ 37 b) sowie den aus dem Obliquus durch eins der Suffixe -ke, -te, -tər, -sa [...] gebildeten Kasusformen (§ 38) ist die dem Suffix unmittelbar vorausgehende Silbe die stärkst betonte [...]. § 5. In den § 4 nicht angeführten Kasusformen, nämlich im Nominativ, Objektiv sowie den Vokativformen ohne -ja, -je, -le, wird, von den § 6 erwähnten Ausnahmen abgesehn, die erste Silbe am stärksten hervorgehoben, z. B. o báro rai 'der Richter' [...], mála 'Kamerad, Freund!', máro 'Brot', štíləpen 'Gefängnis' u. s. w.
new_statements.translation: § 4. In the vocative forms built with one of the suffixes -ja, -je, -le (§ 37b) and in the case forms built from the oblique with one of the suffixes -ke, -te, -tər, -sa [...] (§ 38), the syllable immediately preceding the suffix is the most strongly stressed [...]. § 5. In the case forms not listed in § 4, namely the nominative, objective, and the vocative forms without -ja, -je, -le, apart from the exceptions mentioned in § 6, the first syllable is most strongly prominent, e.g. o báro rai 'the judge' [...], mála 'comrade, friend!', máro 'bread', štíləpen 'prison', etc.
new_statements.citation: Finck, Franz Nikolaus (1903). Lehrbuch des Dialekts der deutschen Zigeuner. Marburg: N. G. Elwert.
new_statements.locator: Zweites Kapitel, A. Stärkeabstufung, § 4-5, p. 5 (PDF p. 27); verbs § 3, p. 4; exceptions § 6, pp. 5-6; uninflected words § 7, p. 7
new_statements.reading: German Sinti (Sinte Romani) as described by Finck in 1903 has morphologically conditioned stress: the citation/nominative form of nouns and most uninflected words carry INITIAL stress (a German-style shift away from the conservative Romani final stress noted by Matras 2006), while Layer-II case forms and -ja/-je/-le vocatives stress the syllable right before the suffix (i.e. the oblique-stem final), present-tense verbs stress the theme vowel before the person ending, and preterites stress the final person suffix; German loan verbs keep German stress. There are listed lexical exceptions (nouns in -kəro, long penults, -itsa, and a word list such as amáro, rašái, sonakái). For catalog purposes: not a fixed-position system; initial-stress default in citation forms with morphological (suffix-preceding / final) stress in inflected forms and lexical exceptions.

sources.citation: Finck, Franz Nikolaus (1903). Lehrbuch des Dialekts der deutschen Zigeuner. Marburg: N. G. Elwert. [first-hand grammar of German Sinti; found in this sweep via archive.org, not in the item list]
sources.quote: § 5. In den § 4 nicht angeführten Kasusformen, nämlich im Nominativ, Objektiv sowie den Vokativformen ohne -ja, -je, -le, wird, von den § 6 erwähnten Ausnahmen abgesehn, die erste Silbe am stärksten hervorgehoben, z. B. o báro rai 'der Richter' (d. h. 'der grosse Herr'), e báre rájes 'den Richter, dem Richter', mála 'Kamerad, Freund!', máro 'Brot', štíləpen 'Gefängnis' u. s. w.
sources.locator: Zweites Kapitel, A. Stärkeabstufung, §§ 3-7, pp. 4-7 (PDF pp. 26-29)
sources.note: Chapter 2 'Das Lautgefüge', A. 'Stärkeabstufung' (§§ 2-8, pp. 4-7) is a full statement of word stress in German Sinti. Verbs (§ 3, p. 4): imperative and a-stem presents stress the root (first) syllable; consonant-/e-stem presents stress the theme vowel immediately before the person ending (an-á-wa, an-é-la); preterite stresses the last syllable (the person suffix: hund-óm, hund-ás); German loan verbs with Romani suffix keep German stress (Anm. 1); imperfect/pluperfect stress the syllable before -es (Anm. 3). Nouns (§ 4, p. 5): vocatives in -ja/-je/-le and Layer-II case forms in -ke/-te/-tər/-…
